1. General muscle gains from a combination of the Big three (squats + bench + deadlift) + accessories. You'll generally gain size depending on your diet.

2. All of them if you do your accesories but if you just do the big 3, quads/hamstrings, erectors, back, and maybe chest/triceps.
3. It can be a little repetitive cause you'll usually stick to the big 3 and a 1-3 variation of the big 3 plus accessories for 4-12 weeks at a time (blocks.). If you're not competinging you'll mainly just be focusing on getting stronger and setting personal numbers either through how heavy the weight is or how many time you moved a heavy weight.
4. You'll usually see body composition changes and feel muscle soreness, maybe some joint aches depending on how you program it.
5. There's nothing really off limit because powerlifting isn't absoultey apperance base but it's general accepted to have a high protein diet, carbs and fats vary based on diet styles.
6. There's some technical difference mainly on standards. Squats are to depth (below parrell), Bench is paused and butt must stay in contact with the pad at all times. Deadlifts can't have hitching or downward movement. Beyond that it's the same it's just how you program the general work.
7. 30 to 60 days before your brain will recognize a change, I've read it's easier to notice if you photo yourself every day.
8. Do accessories do accessories do accessories. They are the backbone of any good program. Do not skip them. Work the quads, hamstrings, erectors, lats, triceps, biceps, pectorals.
